Also qualifying at the final-state/selection-requirement level:
- 2004.14060 (all-hadronic ttbar + MET channel with 1–2 b-tagged jets; SRA/SRB/SRC/SRD regions require b-tagged jets)

question: Which analyses have a ttZ background and a control region used to normalise that background?

answer.text:
Five analyses have a ttZ (t tbar + Z) background together with a control region used to normalise that background:

• 2004.14060 — "$t\bar{t}+Z$ background" → "Control-region-based background normalisation via simultaneous profile likelihood fit", using region hepkg:region:crttz (CRTTZ, 3-lepton with Z mass window).
• 2006.05880 — hepkg:background:ttZ-3l → "Control-region normalisation via profile-likelihood fit, extrapolated to the SR", using hepkg:object:CR-Z-ttZ (CR^Z_ttZ, 3ℓ), with VR^Z_ttZ as validation region.
• 2110.11231 — hepkg:background:ttz-tzq → "MC-based prediction with free-floating normalization constrained via dedicated control region in combined fit", using hepkg:region:cr-ttz (CR-ttZ).
• 2202.08676 — hepkg:background:ttz → "Normalization to data in dedicated control regions", using hepkg:region:3l-ttz-cr (3ℓ ttZ CR; measured λ_ttZ ≈ 1.16 ± 0.15).
• 2401.05299 — "$t\bar{t}Z/\gamma^*$ background" → "Likelihood-fit normalisation factors from control regions", using hepkg:region:3l-ttz-cr (3ℓ ttZ control region).

Borderline cases not counted: 2106.14246 defines a ttZ-enriched control region but records its ttX (tttt/ttH/ttW/ttZ) background as a direct simulation-based estimate; 2012.08600 lumps ttZ with VZ in a "Z+X" background only "normalized/validated" in trilepton/4-lepton CRs. Papers mentioning ttZ with pure MC/theory normalisation (2009.04363, 2103.04956, 2107.12553, 2209.07327, 2309.14442, 2405.18661, 2509.22535) or treating ttZ as the signal (2312.04450) do not qualify.

question: Which analyses require exactly two electrons OR exactly two muons as alternative selections -- parallel ee and mumu channels, rather than requiring both?

answer.text:
Four analyses build their selection as "exactly two electrons" OR "exactly two muons" — parallel same-flavour ee and μμ channels, rather than requiring both flavours (an eμ pair) or only one of them:

• 2506.13565 — high-mass dilepton + b-tagged jets: regions labelled "ℓ+ℓ− (ee or μμ) + 0 / exactly 1 / ≥2 b-tagged jets" (hepkg:final-state:dilepton-0b/1b/2b), with the observable "Dilepton invariant mass (m_ll) spectrum in ee and mumu channels" and the ratio R(mumu/ee) (hepkg:region:dl_eeMumu_1b_excl, dl_eeMumu_2b_incl).

• 2509.22535 — simultaneous charm/bottom Yukawa probe in ttH: the 2-lepton category carries both hepkg:object_selection:electron_2L ("2L channel electron selection") and hepkg:object_selection:muon_2L ("2L channel muon selection") under the shared hepkg:object_selection:lepton_req_2L "two opposite-charge leptons requirement".

• 2511.11853 — Z' -> mu mu search: a dimuon channel with its own signal/control regions (SR_b, SR_{b+j/b}, CR_j, CR_2j) mirrored by a dielectron channel with parallel regions (CR_b^{ee}, CR_{b+j/b}^{ee}, CR_j^{ee}, CR_2j^{ee}).

• 2011.07812 — displaced-lepton search: final state "Two displaced leptons (ee, mumu, or emu)" organised into separate SR-ee (plus VR-ee-fake and VR-ee-heavy-flavor) and SR-mumu regions, each requiring a same-flavour pair.

Ruled out: 2009.04363 and 2602.18611 are muon-only (H->mu mu with no electron counterpart); 2205.05120 mentions "Z->ee/mumu+jets" only as a generated background sample, not as an analysis selection; 2401.07090 runs separate electron and muon B-decay modes but to form the R(K) double ratio rather than as alternative signal selections.

question: Which analyses use b-tagged jets (jets identified as containing a b-hadron) in their event selection?

answer.text:
**48 of the 60 analyses in the graph use b-tagged jets (jets identified as containing a b-hadron) in their event selection.**

How I found them: b-tagging is spread over several entity kinds, so I looked at all of them rather than filtering on one. The evidence lives in `entity_occurrence` rows of kind `detector_object` (e.g. "b-tagged jet (MV2c10)", "b-tagged jet (DeepCSV)", "b-tagged jet (DL1r)", "b-tagged jet (DeepJet)", "b-tagged AK4 jet (ParticleNet b tagging)", "Bottom (b)-tagged jet"), `event_region` (e.g. "SR_b: 1-jet dimuon signal region with exactly one b-tagged jet", "Single-/Double-b-tagged signal region", "SRA/SRB/SRC b tag"), `channel` (e.g. "≥3 leptons + jets/b-jets + MET", "Diphoton + ≥3 jets (≥1 b-tagged)") and `selection_requirement` (e.g. "Baseline b-tagged jet multiplicity requirement", "b-jet eta acceptance and DL1r tagging working points"). Crucially, the labels are not uniformly spelled: many appear as LaTeX `$b$-tagged jet`, which a plain `LIKE '%b-tag%'` misses, so I normalised `$`/braces out of the labels before matching. I then confirmed each candidate with selection-bearing assertions (`object_has_selection`, `region_requires_object`, `result_defines_object`, `region_vetoes_object`, `region_has_selection`, `result_has_channel`, `channel_has_region`), all 48 of which have such links, and cross-checked against the `hepkg:object:b-jet` canonical cluster (38 papers).

The analyses (arXiv ids):
2001.06899, 2004.04545, 2004.14060, 2006.05880, 2007.02873, 2008.05928, 2009.04363, 2010.14293, 2012.03799, 2012.08600, 2102.01444, 2103.04956, 2103.06956, 2106.01676, 2106.14246, 2107.12553, 2109.13808, 2110.11231, 2111.08340, 2112.03161, 2201.11585, 2202.08676, 2205.05120, 2206.09466, 2207.00348, 2208.12095, 2209.07327, 2211.08028, 2302.05225, 2303.15340, 2307.01094, 2308.02285, 2309.14442, 2312.04450, 2401.05299, 2402.08486, 2403.01556, 2405.18661, 2407.10549, 2503.19420, 2506.13565, 2508.13900, 2509.22535, 2510.07527, 2511.11853, 2602.18611, 2604.21670, 2604.27044

question: Which analyses use the HistFitter framework for their statistical analysis?

answer.text:
Five analyses use the HistFitter framework for their statistical treatment (entities hepkg:method:histfitter, hepkg:method:profile-likelihood-fit-histfitter, and the HistFitter-validated pyhf combination hepkg:method:pyhf-combination, linked via result_uses_statistical_method):

- 2006.05880 — per-SR background from a profile-likelihood fit implemented in HistFitter; CL_s intervals from HistFitter's profile-likelihood-ratio test statistic.
- 2011.07812 — "The HistFitter package is used for statistical interpretation", with systematics as Gaussian nuisance parameters.

question: Which analyses unfold their measured distributions -- that is, correct them back to particle level or truth level?

answer.text:
Sixteen analyses unfold their measured distributions back to particle/parton/generator level. Evidence comes from unfolding algorithms attached to results via result_uses_statistical_method, plus source text on response/migration-matrix correction:

- 2001.06899 — TUnfold least-squares unfolding of differential distributions (particle-level fiducial phase space)
- 2103.04956 — unfolding of detector effects from the observed H→4ℓ distributions, repeated with varied response matrices
- 2110.11231 — TUnfold least-squares regularized unfolding with area constraint (differential WZ, particle-level fiducial)
- 2112.00895 — cross sections unfolded to the parton level (W+c)
- 2206.09466 — STXS results unfolded to generator level
- 2207.12246 — iterative dynamically-stabilized unfolding of the t-spectrum, SVD cross-check, MC migration matrix
- 2208.12095 — Fully Bayesian Unfolding, with parton-level top/lepton definitions
- 2303.15340 — bin-by-bin unfolding of eμ differential fiducial cross sections to particle level
- 2308.02285 — explicit "unfolding of measurements to particle and parton levels" (separate particle-level and parton-level sections)
- 2309.14442 — binned maximum-likelihood unfolding ("Unfolding methodology", normalized differential cross sections)
- 2312.04450 — profile-likelihood unfolding (PLU) with Tikhonov regularisation
- 2401.05299 — profile-likelihood unfolding with Tikhonov regularisation and Asimov closure/bias tests
- 2402.08486 — TUnfold χ²-fit unfolding with Tikhonov regularization plus pseudo-data closure test
- 2404.06204 — iterative Bayesian (D'Agostini) unfolding of W and Z pT spectra
- 2504.13081 — combined unfolded differential cross sections (pT^H, pT^j1, N_jets, |y_H|, |Δη_jj|, m_jj, τ_C^j)
- 2506.13565 — TUnfold bin-by-bin migration correction of the high-mass dilepton spectrum

Excluded on inspection: 2405.18661 and 2604.21670 are review/interpretation documents that use other experiments' already-unfolded distributions rather than unfolding themselves; 2106.14246 and 2401.07090 mention "unfolding" only in reference titles (PHYSTAT proceedings, sPlot). The rest of the 60-paper corpus has no unfolding method or text evidence.

Papers: 2001.06899, 2207.12246, 2208.12095, 2308.02285, 2309.14442, 2312.04450, 2401.05299, 2402.08486, 2404.06204, 2405.18661, 2504.13081, 2604.21670

question: Which analyses have a ttZ background and a control region used to normalise that background?

answer.text:
Analyses with a ttZ background AND a control region used to normalise that background:

1. 2004.14060 — ATLAS all-hadronic tt+MET stop search: "$t\bar{t}+Z$ background" normalised via "Control-region-based background normalisation via simultaneous profile likelihood fit", using region hepkg:region:crttz (CRTTZ, 3-lepton, charge sum ±1).
2. 2006.05880 — ATLAS top-squark (H/Z) search: hepkg:background:ttZ-3l normalised by hepkg:method:cr-normalisation-fit (CR profile-likelihood fit extrapolated to SR), with hepkg:object:CR-Z-ttZ ("Control region CR^Z_ttZ for ttZ background normalisation") plus VR^Z_ttZ.
3. 2110.11231 — hepkg:background:ttz-tzq constrained by hepkg:method:mc-cr-constrained-freefloat using hepkg:region:cr-ttz (CR-ttZ).
4. 2202.08676 — hepkg:background:ttz normalised "to data in dedicated control regions" (hepkg:method:cr-normalization) via hepkg:region:3l-ttz-cr; has hepkg:systematic:ttz-normalization.
5. 2401.05299 — ATLAS ttW measurement: "$t\bar{t}Z/\gamma^*$ background" gets "Likelihood-fit normalisation factors from control regions" via the "3L ttZ control region".

Partial case: 2012.08600 — ttZ is folded into hepkg:background:z_plus_x ("Z+X background (VZ, ttZ…)"), which is "Simulation-based estimate normalized/validated in dedicated trilepton and 4-lepton data control regions", so the CR normalisation applies to a ttZ-containing group rather than to ttZ alone.

Excluded because ttZ is present but not CR-normalised: 2009.04363 (parametric mmm fit), 2103.04956 and 2106.01676 (direct MC, explicitly no CR normalisation), 2106.14246 (has a ttZ-enriched CR but ttX background asserted as direct simulation estimate), 2107.12553 (ttZ MC sample; top background from low-m_CT CR), 2312.04450, 2209.07327, 2405.18661, 2509.22535, 2309.14442, 2112.03161, 2508.13900.

question: Which analyses require exactly two electrons OR exactly two muons as alternative selections -- parallel ee and mumu channels, rather than requiring both?

answer.text:
Four analyses treat e⁺e⁻ and μ⁺μ⁻ as alternative (OR) selections requiring exactly two leptons of a single flavour:

• 2511.11853 — mirror-image channels: hepkg:channel:dimuon "Dimuon (mu+mu-) channel" with SR_b, SR_{b+j/b}, CR_j, CR_2j, and hepkg:channel:dielectron "Dielectron (e+e-) control channel" with CR_j^{ee}, CR_2j^{ee}, CR_b^{ee}, CR_{b+j/b}^{ee}.
• 2506.13565 — final states hepkg:final-state:dilepton-0b / -1b / -2b, written as "ℓ+ℓ− (ee or μμ) + 0 / exactly 1 / ≥2 b-tagged jets"; the dilepton mass observable is measured "in ee and mumu channels, by b-tagged jet multiplicity", and events with more than two electrons or two muons are reduced to the best-mass pair.
• 2208.12095 — hepkg:region:dl_eeMumu_1b_excl and hepkg:region:dl_eeMumu_2b_incl, "Dilepton ee+μμ" regions, i.e. the ee and μμ samples combined as alternatives.
• 2509.22535 — a 2-lepton channel implemented with parallel, alternative object selections hepkg:object_selection:electron_2L ("2L channel electron selection") and hepkg:object_selection:muon_2L ("2L channel muon selection") under the shared "two opposite-charge leptons" requirement.

Not included: 2102.01444 and 2006.05880, which accept two leptons of any flavour (ee, μμ or eμ), and 2402.08486 / 2304.08962, where "two electrons or two muons" appears only as a trigger condition.
